projects.title: Poyraz UI Kit
projects.description: A brutalist, open-source React component library built with Tailwind CSS and Radix UI. Features square corners, dashed borders, and bold typography. Designed to provide a unique, raw aesthetic while maintaining high accessibility and usability standards.
projects.problem: Modern UI libraries often look too similar, suffering from "Bootstrap" or "Tailwind" fatigue. Developers crave a design system that feels raw, authentic, and stands out without sacrificing the developer experience or accessibility.
projects.solution: Poyraz UI Kit bridges this gap by offering a brutalist aesthetic built on top of the headless primitives of Radix UI.
projects.role: Lead Designer & Main Maintainer. Responsible for the entire lifecycle from Figma design to React architecture and documentation.
projects.designProcess: The design process began with an exploration of neo-brutalist and retro-web aesthetics. 1. Moodboarding: Collected references from poster designs and architectural brutalism. 2. Tokens: Defined design tokens for spacing, typography, and high-contrast colors. 3. Component Design: Prototyped in Figma, iterating on border widths and shadow offsets. 4. Implementation: Translated Figma designs into Tailwind CSS utility classes.
projects.technicalDetails: The library is structured as a monorepo using Turborepo to manage the core package, documentation site, and example apps. Built with React 18 and Radix UI primitives. Uses tsup for bundling to ESM and CJS formats.
projects.lessonsLearned: Headless UI separation allows for rapid visual iteration without breaking functionality. Configuring bundlers for ESM/CJS compatibility across Next.js versions is a significant challenge.
